title: Northern boys soccer returns after one-year hiatus | Garrett Sports | wvnews.com
text:
ACCIDENT — When the Northern boys’ soccer program was unable to field a team last year, the future seemed uncertain.
Thankfully, that uncertainty may have all but disappeared.
The Huskies return with a healthy roster of 20 kids — 12 of whom are underclassmen.
“We have lots of areas of improvement to make, but I’m just so proud of everybody who has come out, and we even got a couple players that played football last year to come out and play soccer,” Northern coach Jen Upole said. “We also have kids who haven’t touched a soccer ball since youth league, and some of them are juniors, but we appreciate all of them.”
It can be tough to restart a program after a shutdown, but there was no lack of interest. It was also helped that the roster got an immediate boost from the incoming freshmen class which fills out 10 of the spots.
However, Upole was quick to give credit to another fall sports program that helped maintain interest for the boys who were left without a soccer team last year.
“The cross country coach came to us and said to bring them all over that way can still talk the talk, and then on Thursdays or Fridays at practice, he’d let them just get a soccer ball and play a pick-up game on the side,” Upole said. “Things like that really kept them engaged, and they were able to just have something to do, and I have to give him so much credit for standing behind them for their love of soccer.
“And our boys took running cross country seriously. They were willing to support another sport because that’s what you have to do at Northern. When you want programs to survive, that’s what you have to do. You have to help each other.”
Northern will also get help from its four seniors — Richard Deatelhauser, Brady Garlitz, Jacob Kilduff and Ayden Gormley. Coach Upole noted that Deatelhauser, Garlitz and Kilduff are captains while Gormley is returning to soccer for the first time since playing in youth leagues.
“They’ve been great leaders and they’ve also added some size to our lineup, and we need that because when you have such a young lineup that lacks size you’d expect them to get knocked around on the field a little bit, but I think their leadership (from the upperclassmen) is sort of bringing everybody together,” Upole said. “We also have a freshman at goalkeeper. He’s a tall kid and he’s figuring it out, but for all these young guys, they haven’t had a JV season under their belt before being thrown to the wolves at the varsity level. Their last experience was JCP, AYSO or MSA.
“The foundation for what you want in the team is definitely there, but this will come down to how we face the ups and downs of moving through the regular season and how we start on Saturday.”
The WestMAC is expected to be a gauntlet once again this year as well as the region playoffs, but the Huskies know that the built-in strength of schedule is already there.
“We just can’t let up, no matter what,” Upole said. “Everybody just has to dig deep and find out what you’re made of. When you think you can’t run or take another step, you have to find a way. You have to push. The reason you push harder is because you have 19 other teammates that are doing that, and you’re always running and offering some sort of encouragement.
“It’ll be a tough thing to fight through, but we’re all going to come out tougher in the end.”
One match in particular that will be a highlight for fans comes late in the season when the Huskies host the Southern Rams at 9:30 a.m. in front of the student body on Thursday Oct. 8, during Autumn Glory week.
“We’ve already been talking about it, and I hope the student body gets really into that,” Upole said. “I hope the boys get over the nerves real quick and just get that to business. It’s great for the county, I think it’ll be fun for everybody.”
Listed below is the roster of the 2026 Northern boys’ soccer team whose interest in the program led to the quick revival of the prgoram:
Seniors: Richard Deatelhauser, Brady Garlitz, Ayden Gormley and Jacob Kilduff.
Juniors: Hosea Gormley, Brody Shaffer, Brayden Upole and Peyton Yoder.
Sophomores: August Cain and Zach Fogle.
Freshmen: Yonatan Benitez, Lawson Call, Ben Kamp, Joey Major, Grady Miller, Bode Panther, Cash VanSickle, Jacob Varchetti, Charlie Williams and Owen Workman.
